solution: Building i is visible exactly when h_i exceeds every earlier height, so a prefix is summarised by (running maximum H, number visible so far) and the DP is over those states. With H fixed, an invisible building is cheapest at h_i = min(p_i, H), costing c_i*max(0, p_i - H) and leaving H alone (and it is illegal while H = 0, since heights are positive, which is why building 1 is always visible); a visible building may take any height above H and becomes the new maximum. The trap is that a visible building is NOT always best at max(p_i, H+1): lowering it below its preferred height can be worth it so a later cheap building can still clear it, so the candidate heights are p_j + d for |d| <= n - O(n^2) values - and the visible transition is evaluated with a prefix minimum over the running-maximum axis. That gives O(n^2 * n^2) = O(n^4) time at n = 70 and O(n^3) memory rolled to two layers; the answer is the cheapest state with at least k visible.
statement_summary: Positive integer heights must be chosen for n buildings standing in a row, where building i costs its cost factor times the distance from its preferred height. A building is visible from the tram at position zero when it is strictly taller than every building before it, and the task is the cheapest assignment making at least k of the n buildings visible.
notes: Verified on the statement sample and 300 random cases (n <= 5) against exhaustive enumeration of all height vectors. My first DP - visible buildings snap to max(p_i, H+1) - passed the sample but the brute force killed it immediately: P=[4,4,1,1], C=[1,3,4,4], k=2 costs 1 by LOWERING building 1 to 3 so that building 2 at its own preferred height 4 is visible; the greedy DP paid 3. Hence candidates must extend below p_j as well as above. No binary-search-answer and no greedy: the exchange only holds inside the DP. longest-increasing-subsequence is listed at low confidence because the visible set is exactly an increasing subsequence of heights, but the cost structure, not the length, is the problem.
